title: Lefschetz pencils, nearby cycles and vanishing cycles, Part II: prescribed finite-field points
summary: Construct a smooth geometrically integral affine curve through a prescribed rational point of a scheme smooth near that point, meeting a chosen dense open over the original field. A bounded polynomial graph and its étale pullback replace a projective Bertini argument. This supplies the local same-field curve input to Kisin–Zhou, beyond the parent’s finite-extension existence result.
readme:
# Prescribed finite-field points

This Part II adds the one-point same-field curve supplier to the parent’s LPV.3 finite-extension pencil existence. Its two layers use the existing multivariate polynomial, spectrum, étale and geometric-integrality carriers. FC.0 constructs a bounded-exponent graph through zero and proves coefficient preservation and avoidance. FC.1 pulls it back along an étale chart and retains the rational marked component. The zero-dimensional case uses a constant map from A¹.

The full reader is research/blueprint/readmes/LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCyclesPartII.md. All fields are allowed; the finite-field application keeps the residue field and Frobenius power unchanged. General smooth coordinates, boundary-image dimension and marked-component geometry are imported from SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0. Projective or multipoint Bertini, pencils, stack-atlas lifting, singular local-model root subgroups, hypersurface monodromy and semistable potential maps have their separate owners. The packet records the issue-authorized allocation of the last two directions.

stages.title: Polynomial graphs over the original field
stages.description: Define φ(m,B):k[X₀,…,Xₘ₋₁]→k[T], X_i↦T^(B^i), using Mathlib evaluation. Prove bounded-support coefficient preservation via existing base-B digit uniqueness and surjectivity for m>0. For nonzero h choose B≥2 exceeding every individual support exponent; its graph is a closed immersion through zero with nonzero substituted polynomial, and over a field meets D(h) densely. Include the m=0 boundary, the one-variable identification, F₂ rational-line failure and the wrong-base collision. This is polynomial nonvanishing, not a point-counting assertion. The reader gives the complete graph API and tests.

stages.title: Marked étale curves through prescribed points
stages.description: For an integral affine chart π:V→A^m over k, m>0, mark y∈V(k) over zero, contain the image of V∖U in V(h), and pull back the FC.0 graph. Select the connected component through (y,0); prove it affine, étale over A¹, smooth of relative dimension one, geometrically integral and with dense inverse image of U. Export a k-curve morphism through any k-rational smooth point with U dense on its component. Treat dimension zero by a constant A¹ map. Over F_q retain residue degree one. Import general coordinates and rational-point component geometry from SF.0; no projectivity, multiple-point or full Shimura result is asserted.
